steps.text: Pat the thighs dry and salt both sides. Lay them skin side down in the hot sunflower oil and leave them alone until the skin is deep golden and lifts off the pan by itself.
Turn the thighs, lower the heat and cook the other side. Check the thickest thigh against a trusted guide to doneness, then move them to a warm plate.
Pour off most of the fat and keep every brown bit. Stir the garlic in the pan just until it smells sweet.
Pour in the white wine and scrape the pan with a wooden spoon until the brown bits have dissolved.
Let it boil until about half is left.
Take the pan off the heat. Whisk in the cold butter a few cubes at a time, then the juice of the lemon. The sauce turns glossy.
Taste, and add salt if it needs it. Pour the sauce into a warm jug.
Wilt the spinach in the same pan.
Plate the spinach with the chicken, skin side up, and spoon the sauce around it.

Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the salt and whisk until no streaks of white are left.

Melt most of the butter in a small pan over low heat until it foams, and keep the rest cold. Pour in the eggs and stir without stopping, scraping the bottom and the corners. Lift the pan off the heat whenever curds form too fast.
While the eggs still look wet and loose, take the pan off the heat and stir in the cold butter and the cream to stop the cooking. Serve at once on warm plates.

Melt most of the butter in a small pan over low heat until it foams, and keep the rest cold. Pour in the eggs and stir without stopping, scraping the bottom and the corners. Lift the pan off the heat whenever curds form too fast.
While the eggs still look wet and loose, take the pan off the heat and stir in the cold butter and the crème fraîche to stop the cooking. Serve at once on warm plates.
Crack the eggs into a bowl with the salt and the black pepper, and whisk only until the streaks of white are gone.
Melt half the butter in the pan over medium heat. Turn the spinach in it until it collapses, then tip it onto a plate and press out the water.
Wipe the pan and melt the rest of the butter until it foams. Pour in the eggs and stir fast in small circles, shaking the pan, until they are mostly set and still wet on top.
Stop stirring and let the bottom firm for a moment. Scatter the spinach and the vegetarian hard cheese down the middle.
Tilt the pan, fold the near edge over the filling and roll the omelette to the far lip. Turn it out onto a warm plate, seam side down.
